text: And one thing we realized working with those companies is that the ones that successfully manage to ship reliable agents and also continuously improve them follow something that we call like some form of this, the AI engineering loop.

text: And it is about a set of practices that help you to continuously improve your system by taking a systematic approach.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: The foundation to this is always tracing.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Tracing is about getting all the steps of what your agent is doing into a more or less lock, but ideally also in a way you can inspect it as a human.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Monitoring is about finding the interesting ones, so what is going wrong, what is going right, where should we look deeper into, but also understanding how is it performing on average.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Building datasets is about finding a representative set of examples that you want your application to be able to handle, and also how you want it to handle it.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And then you want to run experiments on it, so try different variations of your system to check how it is performing, how it's going, and then of course you want to evaluate how it's going.

text: So for traces, the most important goal is that you want to get deep insights into what your agent is actually doing.

speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: This is then the foundation to track the cost, the latency, the tokens involved, and also have a log to inspect for you as a human to really dig into what's going on, but also for your coding agents to work with it and look at it at scale and just have this inspectable log of what's actually been going on.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Monitoring is then about making sense of it at scale, because especially now with increasing automation levels, longer traces, and a lot of use cases, it's just not feasible anymore for you as a human to look through those logs completely manually, but you actually want a way to get aggregate metrics on what's actually going on.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And also detect signals where things are going wrong.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So for example, cost and latency metrics, but maybe also quality signals like our compliance guardrails kept true to, also like how many users are actually frustrated with our system, how many are writing all caps messages because they are maybe a bit upset with what the agent just did.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And yeah, all of this aggregating and then of course also finding the interesting stuff that you want to dig deeper into.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: What you get from production through this monitoring is then also one of the foundations that you can use to build out your datasets.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And datasets are, in the end, a representation of what you want your agent to handle in production.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So all the cases that it might be getting, also maybe out-of-scope requests that you want to correctly also be deferred and make sure that the agent's not trying to give investment advice or also answering what the weather in New York's gonna be like if it's actually just a dead IT support agent.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And those items you can then have like the input but also what you expect it to have as the output which can both be like a sample reply or also expected behavior that you want to see or keywords you want to have covered.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And this can then be used as a stable benchmark either for like improving and iterating offline or also as part of your CICD.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Those datasets are then used to run experiments on, and experiments are, if you maybe look back into university and statistics or anything that you might have done, it's in the end this idea of varying something about your setup and looking what happens then.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So for example, changing a prompt, changing a model, changing the context or the tool description, and to see if it's then better dealing with what you actually want it to deal with, and ideally isolating concerns.

text: So if you want to check if the same model
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Performs better with a different prompt.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: You ideally only change the prompt and not five other things because otherwise it's going to be hard for you to interpret what you actually see.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And then finally, you need evals or evaluation approaches to make sure you can also measure what's happening in those experiments because, again, you don't want to look at everything yourself, which you, by the way, should probably sometimes do, but still you also want the scalable approaches which are, for example, LLM as a judge, so using another LLM to check what the LLM did.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Or also code-based evals for things like classification tasks where you can check for an exact match or also checking behavior can be a deterministic check or if you are checking for all caps type things.

speaker: SPEAKER_01
